text:
Sidney Crosby's second goal on Saturday was a poke from the doorstep with 1:16 left, and it ended a game the Kings had spent most of the night controlling. It also, as Hockey Hot Stove's Ryan Wilson noted, left Crosby alone in sixth on the NHL's all-time scoring list at 1,772 points, past Marcel Dionne, against the franchise Dionne starred for. Pittsburgh won 5-2 and snapped a four-game winless run (0-3-1).

How the Penguins got there is the part they shouldn't look at too closely. Tommy Novak, a 2015 fifth-round pick who was playing in the ECHL as recently as 2020-21, scored twice in the first 5:10. Corey Perry batted one in from close range to make it 2-1, and Los Angeles owned the rest of the period, out-chancing Pittsburgh 1.84 to 0.97 in expected goals (the quality of chances). Then Egor Chinakhov scored on the power play with 29 seconds left in the first, from a spot that goes in about 6 percent of the time.

Alex Laferriere pulled the Kings within one on a second-period power play and finished with seven shots, but Crosby's deflection at 17:13 of the second restored the two-goal lead. Our win probability model rated that the swing goal of the game, moving Pittsburgh from 71 percent to 87. Evgeni Malkin assisted on both Crosby goals and Chinakhov's, a three-point night arriving in the same week as a stack of headlines about him being asked for a list of teams he'd accept a trade to. If this is a farewell tour, he is playing it loud.

The honest verdict: the Kings deserved this one. They outattempted Pittsburgh 71 to 50, had 3.99 expected goals to 2.80, and in our replays of every shot they win 80 percent of the time. The difference was in net. Sergei Murashov stopped 26 of 28, about two goals better than his shots deserved, and made the save of the night on a 23 percent Laferriere chance in the third. Darcy Kuemper allowed four on 18 shots, nearly two worse than expected.

Pittsburgh needed points from somewhere, and the trip west has been rough. It will take this, and Crosby's chase of Ron Francis, 26 points ahead of him, gives the season a thread to follow whatever happens in the standings.
headline: Crosby passes Dionne as Penguins steal one in LA
